records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a new speech, turning from the leaders' gifts back to the sanctuary and its servants
decisions.reason: Chapter 7 ended with Moses hearing the voice speaking to him from above the ark (7:89). This chapter has two instructions: the lamps of the lampstand (verses 1-4) and the setting apart of the Levites for their work (verses 5-26), which carries on from chapter 3 (3:5-13).

records.heading: Setting up the lamps

records.source: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֵלָ֑יו בְּהַעֲלֹֽתְךָ֙ אֶת־הַנֵּרֹ֔ת אֶל־מוּל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמְּנוֹרָ֔ה יָאִ֖ירוּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת הַנֵּרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Speak to Aaron and say to him, when you make go up the lamps, to [the] front of [the] face of the lampstand will give light [the] seven [of] the lamps.
pieces: "Speak to Aaron and tell him, 'When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to shine out toward the front of the lampstand.'"

L.2: "Speak to Aaron and say to him, 'When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light toward the front of the lampstand.'"

R.2: "Tell Aaron, 'When you put the seven lamps in place on the lampstand, set them so that their light falls in front of it.'"

decisions.choice: set up: put the lamps in place and light them
decisions.reason: The verb means "make go up". With lamps it is used for setting them on the lampstand and lighting them, perhaps from the flame that rises (Exodus 25:37; 27:20; 40:25). Either way the point is the same: the priest's daily care of the lamps.

decisions.choice: toward the front of the lampstand: the lamps shine forward into the holy place
decisions.reason: The lamps were small open bowls of oil with a lip for the wick. Turned the same way, they threw their light into the space in front of the lampstand, across the holy place toward the table with the bread (Exodus 25:37; 26:35). The lamps were kept burning from evening to morning (Exodus 27:21; Leviticus 24:2-4).

decisions.choice: put the seven lamps in place ... set them so that their light falls in front of it
decisions.reason: Readable makes the instruction plain: what matters is the direction the lamps face. "In front of it" explains the Hebrew "to the front of the face of".

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן אֶל־מוּל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמְּנוֹרָ֔ה הֶעֱלָ֖ה נֵרֹתֶ֑יהָ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And did so Aaron; to [the] front of [the] face of the lampstand he made go up its lamps, as commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: Aaron carried this out, setting up its lamps toward the front of the lampstand, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.3: And Aaron did so; he set up its lamps toward the front of the lampstand, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses.

R.3: Aaron did what he was told. He set up the lamps so they shone toward the front of the lampstand. He did it just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses.

decisions.choice: as the LORD commanded Moses: Aaron's obedience matches the command exactly
decisions.reason: The book often closes an instruction by saying that it was carried out just as the LORD commanded (1:54; 2:34). Here the command came to Aaron through Moses, and Aaron did exactly what was said.

records.source: וְזֶ֨ה מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה הַמְּנֹרָה֙ מִקְשָׁ֣ה זָהָ֔ב עַד־יְרֵכָ֥הּ עַד־פִּרְחָ֖הּ מִקְשָׁ֣ה הִ֑וא כַּמַּרְאֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶרְאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And this [was the] work of the lampstand: hammered work [of] gold, to its base to its blossom hammered work [was] it; like the appearance that showed Yahweh Moses, so he made the lampstand.
pieces: The lampstand was crafted like this: it was hammered work in gold, beaten out from its base to its blossoms. It was made in keeping with the pattern that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had shown Moses.

L.4: And this [was] the workmanship of the lampstand: hammered work of gold; from its base to its blossoms it [was] hammered work. According to the pattern that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had shown Moses, so he made the lampstand.

R.4: The lampstand was made of gold, hammered into shape all the way from its base to the flower shapes at the top. It was made to follow the design {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had shown Moses.

decisions.choice: hammered work: beaten out of one piece of gold, not cast in parts
decisions.reason: The word names metal beaten into shape. Exodus 25:31-36 says the lampstand with its branches, cups and blossoms was beaten out of one talent of pure gold, all of one piece.

decisions.choice: from its base to its blossoms: the whole lampstand, from bottom to top
alternatives: from its shaft to its flowers
decisions.reason: The first word can mean the base or the central stem; the second names the flower-shaped cups that held the lamps (Exodus 25:31, 33). Together they mean the lampstand from one end to the other.

decisions.choice: the pattern the LORD had shown Moses: the model Moses saw on the mountain
decisions.reason: Exodus 25:9, 40 tells Moses to make the tabernacle and the lampstand by the pattern he was shown on the mountain. The word here is "appearance", what Moses saw.

decisions.choice: he made: the maker is not named
decisions.reason: The verb is "he made" with no subject. Exodus 37:17-24 says Bezalel made the lampstand; the sentence may also mean that Moses had it made. The meaning is the same: it was made as God showed.

decisions.choice: It was made
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "it was made", which leaves the maker unnamed as the Hebrew does. Literal keeps "he made".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a new instruction: the setting apart of the Levites
decisions.reason: The speech that begins here runs to verse 19 and is carried out in verses 20-22. Chapter 3 had already said that the Levites were to belong to the LORD in place of the firstborn (3:11-13, 40-51); here they are made ready for that work.

records.heading: The Levites are made clean and presented

records.source: קַ֚ח אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִתּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְטִהַרְתָּ֖ אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Take the Levites from among [the] sons of Israel and cleanse them.
pieces: "Take the Levites from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and make them clean.

L.6: "Take the Levites from among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and cleanse them.

R.6: "Take the Levites from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and make them clean.

decisions.choice: cleanse: make clean, fit to come near what is holy
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for clean and unclean throughout Leviticus. To be clean is not about dirt but about being fit to come near the LORD's dwelling (Leviticus 11-15). The Levites are not priests and are not anointed or made holy as Aaron and his sons were (Leviticus 8); they are made clean so they can handle the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: from among: chosen out of the people and set apart from them
decisions.reason: The Levites are taken out of the whole people. Verse 14 says the purpose: they are to be separated and to belong to the LORD.

decisions.choice: make them clean
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "make clean" so that the link with "clean" and "unclean" stays clear. Literal has the one word "cleanse".

records.source: וְכֹֽה־תַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְטַֽהֲרָ֔ם הַזֵּ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֵ֣י חַטָּ֑את וְהֶעֱבִ֤ירוּ תַ֨עַר֙ עַל־כָּל־בְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְכִבְּס֥וּ בִגְדֵיהֶ֖ם וְהִטֶּהָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And thus you will do to them to cleanse them: sprinkle on them water of sin-offering, and they will make pass a razor over all their flesh, and they will wash their clothes and cleanse themselves.
pieces: This is what you are to do to make them clean: sprinkle them with the water of purification. Then they are to pass a razor over their whole body, wash their clothes, and make themselves clean.

L.7: And thus you shall do to them to cleanse them: sprinkle on them water of purification, and they shall pass a razor over all their flesh, and they shall wash their clothes and cleanse themselves.

R.7: This is how you will make them clean. Sprinkle the special water that takes away sin on them. Then they must shave off all the hair on their bodies and wash their clothes. In this way they will be clean.

decisions.choice: water of purification: water that takes away sin and uncleanness
alternatives: water for the removal of sin
decisions.reason: The phrase is "water of sin" or "water of sin offering". The word for sin offering also means the removing of sin, and this water was used to cleanse. The text does not say how it was prepared. The water made with the ashes of the red cow in chapter 19 is called by a different name (19:9), so they may not be the same.

decisions.choice: pass a razor over all their flesh: shave the whole body
decisions.reason: Shaving all the hair marked a new start after uncleanness; a person healed of a skin disease did the same (Leviticus 14:8-9). Here it prepares the Levites to begin their work.

decisions.choice: cleanse themselves: the Levites take part in their own cleansing
decisions.reason: The last verb is reflexive. Moses sprinkles them, but the Levites shave, wash and so make themselves clean (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the special water that takes away sin
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name of the water instead of using a term new readers would not know.

records.source: וְלָֽקְחוּ֙ פַּ֣ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֔ר וּמִנְחָת֔וֹ סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשָּׁ֑מֶן וּפַר־שֵׁנִ֥י בֶן־בָּקָ֖ר תִּקַּ֥ח לְחַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And they will take a bull, a son of [the] herd, and its grain offering, fine flour mixed with oil; and a second bull, a son of [the] herd, you will take for a sin offering.
pieces: They are to bring a young bull and the grain offering that goes with it, fine flour mixed with oil. You yourself are to take another young bull as a sin offering.

L.8: And they shall take a bull, a young one of the herd, and its grain offering, fine flour mixed with oil; and a second bull, a young one of the herd, you shall take for a sin offering.

R.8: Then the Levites must bring a young bull, along with a grain offering of fine flour mixed with olive oil. You must also bring a second young bull as a sin offering.

decisions.choice: a bull, a young one of the herd: a young bull
decisions.reason: "Son of the herd" means a young animal from the cattle. A bull was the largest offering, the one brought for the high priest or the whole people (Leviticus 4:3, 14).

decisions.choice: they shall take ... you shall take: the Levites bring one bull, Moses the other
decisions.reason: The verb changes from "they" to "you". The first bull, for the burnt offering (verse 12), is the Levites' own; the second, for the sin offering, is taken by Moses. Verse 12 names what each bull is for.

decisions.choice: its grain offering: the gift of flour and oil that went with a burnt offering
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was usually joined by a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil (15:8-9; Leviticus 2:1-2). "Its" ties it to the first bull.

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: Readable says "olive oil", the oil that was used, for readers who know other kinds.

records.source: וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לִפְנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהִ֨קְהַלְתָּ֔ אֶֽת־כָּל־עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And you will bring near the Levites before [the] tent of meeting, and you will assemble all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Bring the Levites forward in front of the tent of meeting, and call together the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.9: And you shall bring the Levites near before the tent of meeting, and you shall assemble all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.9: Bring the Levites up to the meeting tent. Then call the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} together there.

decisions.choice: before the tent of meeting: at its entrance, where the people could gather
decisions.reason: The people came no further than the courtyard at the tent's entrance (Leviticus 8:3-4). The whole congregation is there because the Levites are being given on their behalf (verses 10-11).

decisions.choice: bring near: present for service
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bringing an offering and for presenting people to serve at the sanctuary (Exodus 29:4; Numbers 3:6). Here the Levites are brought much as an offering is.

records.source: וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֥ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְסָמְכ֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will bring near the Levites before Yahweh, and will lay [the] sons of Israel their hands on the Levites.
pieces: When you have brought the Levites before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are to place their hands on them.

L.10: And you shall bring the Levites near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites.

R.10: Bring the Levites to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must put their hands on the Levites.

decisions.choice: lay their hands on the Levites: name them as their own, given in their place
decisions.reason: When someone brought an animal for an offering, he laid his hand on its head (Leviticus 1:4; 3:2). The people do this to the Levites, who are given to the LORD for them, in place of their firstborn (verses 16-18). The Levites will do the same to the bulls (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: the people as a body, likely through their leaders
decisions.reason: The whole people is named, but it is hard to picture every Israelite laying hands on the Levites. The elders or leaders may have done it for the people, as the elders do for the congregation in Leviticus 4:15.

decisions.choice: When you have brought
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses so that the order of events is clear. Literal and Readable keep two steps.

records.source: וְהֵנִיף֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֤ם תְּנוּפָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָי֕וּ לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will wave Aaron the Levites [as] a wave offering before Yahweh from [the] sons of Israel, and they will be to serve the service of Yahweh.
pieces: Aaron is to present the Levites before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, so that they may do the work of serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: And Aaron shall wave the Levites [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and they shall be [there] to serve the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: Aaron must present the Levites to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. They are a gift from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Then they can take up the work of serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: wave ... as a wave offering: present to the LORD with a gesture of giving
decisions.reason: A wave offering was a part of a gift held out before the LORD and so given to him, and then handed to the priests for their use (Leviticus 7:30-34; Exodus 29:24-27). Here the gift is people: the Levites are given to the LORD, and he gives them to the priests (verse 19). The text does not say what the gesture was when people were presented; it may have been a solemn presenting rather than a movement to and fro.

decisions.choice: serve the service of the LORD: do the work of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word for service covers work of every kind; for the Levites it was looking after the tabernacle and carrying it on the march (3:5-8; 4:4-33). It is service done for the LORD, at his dwelling.

decisions.choice: present ... as a wave offering
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "present" for the verb, because people cannot be waved like a piece of meat, and keep "wave offering" as the name of the offering. Literal has "wave" for the verb as well.

records.source: וְהַלְוִיִּם֙ יִסְמְכ֣וּ אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֔ם עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ הַפָּרִ֑ים וַ֠עֲשֵׂה אֶת־הָאֶחָ֨ד חַטָּ֜את וְאֶת־הָאֶחָ֤ד עֹלָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And the Levites will lay their hands on [the] head of the bulls, and offer the one [as] a sin offering and the one [as] a burnt offering to Yahweh, to make atonement for the Levites.
pieces: The Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. Then offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to make atonement for the Levites.

L.12: And the Levites shall lay their hands on the head of the bulls, and offer the one [as] a sin offering and the other [as] a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to make atonement for the Levites.

R.12: The Levites must put their hands on the heads of the two bulls. Then offer one bull to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. This will make atonement for the Levites.

decisions.choice: offer: a command to Moses, carried out by the priest
decisions.reason: The verb is addressed to "you", Moses, who is in charge of the whole rite. Verse 21 says that Aaron made the atonement, so the priest did the offering itself.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for the Levites: to deal with sin so that they can come near
decisions.reason: The sin offering removes sin and uncleanness, and the burnt offering is given whole to the LORD (Leviticus 1; 4). Both prepare the Levites to serve near the holy things. The sin offering is named first, as in Leviticus 9:7, before the gift that is wholly given.

decisions.choice: lay their hands on the head of the bulls: the animals stand for the Levites
decisions.reason: As the people laid their hands on the Levites (verse 10), the Levites now lay their hands on the bulls offered for them (Leviticus 1:4; 4:4).

records.source: וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י בָנָ֑יו וְהֵנַפְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֛ם תְּנוּפָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And you will make stand the Levites before Aaron and before his sons, and you will wave them [as] a wave offering to Yahweh.
pieces: Set the Levites before Aaron and his sons, and present them to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering.

L.13: And you shall have the Levites stand before Aaron and before his sons, and you shall wave them [as] a wave offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: Make the Levites stand facing Aaron and his sons. Then present them to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering.

decisions.choice: you shall wave them: Moses is in charge, Aaron does it
decisions.reason: Verse 11 says Aaron waves the Levites, and here "you", Moses, does. Moses gives the command and oversees; Aaron carries it out (verse 21).

decisions.choice: before Aaron and his sons: placed under the priests, whom they are to help
decisions.reason: The Levites stand before the priests because they are given to them as helpers (3:6-9; 8:19). Standing before someone often meant serving him (Deuteronomy 10:8; 1 Kings 10:8).

decisions.choice: present them as a wave offering
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.source: וְהִבְדַּלְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִתּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will separate the Levites from among [the] sons of Israel, and will be to me the Levites.
pieces: By doing this you will set the Levites apart from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and the Levites will belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.14: And you shall separate the Levites from among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and the Levites shall be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

R.14: This will make the Levites separate from the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They will be {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

decisions.choice: separate: set apart from others for a purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is used for God dividing light from darkness (Genesis 1:4) and for Israel set apart from the nations (Leviticus 20:24, 26). The Levites are marked off from the other tribes for the LORD's work (Deuteronomy 10:8).

decisions.choice: the Levites shall be mine: they belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: The same words are said in 3:12-13 and 3:45. The Levites are the LORD's own, which is why he can give them to the priests (verse 19).

decisions.choice: By doing this / This will make
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" here sums up what the steps in verses 6-13 bring about. Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְטִֽהַרְתָּ֣ אֹתָ֔ם וְהֵנַפְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם תְּנוּפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And after so will go in the Levites to serve [the] tent of meeting, and you will cleanse them and you will wave them [as] a wave offering.
pieces: After that the Levites may go in to serve at the tent of meeting, once you have made them clean and presented them as a wave offering.

L.15: And after that the Levites shall go in to serve the tent of meeting, and you shall cleanse them and wave them [as] a wave offering.

R.15: First make the Levites clean and present them as a wave offering. After that they can go in and work at the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: and you shall cleanse them: a summary of what must happen first
decisions.reason: The last clauses, "and you shall cleanse them and wave them", come after "go in to serve" but describe what verses 6-13 have already set out. They repeat the conditions: only once the Levites are clean and presented may they begin.

decisions.choice: serve the tent of meeting: do the work of caring for it
decisions.reason: The Levites' work was to look after the tent and its things and to carry it when Israel moved (3:7-8; 4:15, 25-33). They served the tent; the priests served at the altar and in the holy place (18:2-7).

decisions.choice: once you have made them clean / First make the Levites clean
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show these clauses as a condition that comes first in time; Readable puts it first. Literal keeps the Hebrew order and its "and".

records.source: כִּי֩ נְתֻנִ֨ים נְתֻנִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ לִ֔י מִתּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל תַּחַת֩ פִּטְרַ֨ת כָּל־רֶ֜חֶם בְּכ֥וֹר כֹּל֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָקַ֥חְתִּי אֹתָ֖ם לִֽי׃
records.gloss: For given, given [are] they to me from among [the] sons of Israel; in place of [the] first issue of every womb, [the] firstborn of all from [the] sons of Israel, I have taken them for myself.
pieces: They are given over entirely to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. I have taken them for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} in place of the firstborn, the first child born to every mother in Israel.

L.16: For they [are] given, given to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; in place of the first to open every womb, the firstborn of all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, I have taken them for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

R.16: The Levites are given completely to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. I have taken them for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} in place of the firstborn sons, the first son born in each Israelite family.

decisions.choice: given, given: wholly given
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a word to make it stronger. The Levites are not lent or partly given; they are entirely handed over. The same doubled word is used in 3:9.

decisions.choice: the first to open every womb: a woman's first child
decisions.reason: The phrase means the first child a mother bears, here the first son, as in the law of the firstborn (Exodus 13:2, 12; Numbers 3:12). Only males were counted in the exchange (3:40-43).

decisions.choice: in place of: the Levites are exchanged for Israel's firstborn
decisions.reason: The firstborn of Israel belonged to the LORD because he spared them in Egypt (verse 17). Instead of taking every family's firstborn son, he takes the tribe of Levi (3:11-13, 40-51).

decisions.choice: the first to open every womb
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the Hebrew word, the one that "opens" the womb. Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: firstborn sons
decisions.reason: Readable adds "sons", since the exchange concerned the firstborn males (3:40-43).

records.source: כִּ֣י לִ֤י כָל־בְּכוֹר֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה בְּי֗וֹם הַכֹּתִ֤י כָל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם הִקְדַּ֥שְׁתִּי אֹתָ֖ם לִֽי׃
records.gloss: For to me [is] every firstborn among [the] sons of Israel, among man and among beast; on [the] day of my striking every firstborn in [the] land of Egypt I consecrated them for myself.
pieces: For every firstborn among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, of people and of animals alike. I made them holy to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} on the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt.

L.17: For every firstborn among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, among man and among beast; on the day that I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt I made them holy for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.

R.17: Every firstborn in Israel belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, both people and animals. When I killed all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart Israel's firstborn as {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

decisions.choice: the day I struck every firstborn in Egypt: the tenth plague and the Passover
decisions.reason: On the night of the Passover the LORD struck the firstborn of Egypt and passed over Israel's houses (Exodus 12:12-13, 29). From then on Israel's firstborn, of people and of animals, belonged to him (Exodus 13:2, 11-15; Numbers 3:13).

decisions.choice: I consecrated them: made them holy, set apart as his
decisions.reason: The verb means to make holy, to set something apart as belonging to God. The firstborn were the LORD's; firstborn sons were bought back from him (Exodus 13:13; Numbers 18:15-16).

decisions.choice: man and beast: people and animals
decisions.reason: The first word means human beings, not only men. The pair covers every kind of firstborn.

decisions.choice: killed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "struck" means here: the firstborn of Egypt died (Exodus 12:29-30).

records.source: וָאֶקַּח֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם תַּ֥חַת כָּל־בְּכ֖וֹר בִּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: So I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.18: And I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.18: So now I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn: as in verse 16
decisions.reason: The sentence repeats verse 16 and 3:12 to draw the conclusion of verse 17: because the firstborn are the LORD's, he may take the Levites in their place.

records.source: וָאֶתְּנָ֨ה אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֜ם נְתֻנִ֣ים׀לְאַהֲרֹ֣ן וּלְבָנָ֗יו מִתּוֹךְ֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ לַעֲבֹ֞ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וּלְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֨א יִהְיֶ֜ה בִּבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נֶ֔גֶף בְּגֶ֥שֶׁת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And I have given the Levites [as] given ones to Aaron and to his sons from among [the] sons of Israel, to serve [the] service of [the] sons of Israel in [the] tent of meeting and to make atonement for [the] sons of Israel, and not will be among [the] sons of Israel a plague when come near [the] sons of Israel to the holy [place].
pieces: I have handed over the Levites, taken from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, to Aaron and his sons as a gift. They are to do the work of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at the tent of meeting and make atonement for them, so that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are not struck by a plague when they approach the sanctuary."

L.19: And I have given the Levites [as] given ones to Aaron and to his sons from among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to serve the service of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, so that there will be no plague among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel when the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel come near to the sanctuary."

R.19: I have given the Levites to Aaron and his sons as helpers. At the meeting tent they will do the work that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} owe. They will make atonement for the people. Then no deadly sickness will come on the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} when they come near the holy place."

decisions.choice: given ones: given over, as a gift
decisions.reason: The word is the same as in verse 16. The LORD received the Levites as wholly given to him; now he gives them in turn to the priests (3:9; 18:6).

decisions.choice: the service of the sons of Israel: the work owed by Israel, done for them
decisions.reason: The work at the tent belongs to the whole people; the Levites do it on their behalf, in place of the firstborn.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for the sons of Israel: to shield the people from the danger of the holy
alternatives: to make atonement by offering sacrifices
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the Levites camp around the tabernacle and guard it "so that there will be no wrath on the congregation" (1:53; 18:5). By their guarding and their work they keep the people from coming too near the holy things and dying (17:27-28). In this way their service makes atonement, keeping away the punishment that would come on the people.

decisions.choice: plague: a deadly blow from God
decisions.reason: The word means a blow or stroke, used for a plague sent as punishment (Exodus 12:13; Numbers 17:11-12).

decisions.choice: them / they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the people of Israel five times in this verse. Balanced and Readable use "them", "they" or "the people" for some of these so that the sentence reads naturally. Literal keeps every repetition, which stresses that all this is for the people.

decisions.choice: helpers; deadly sickness
decisions.reason: Readable says "helpers" for "given ones", which is what the Levites were to the priests (3:6-9), and "deadly sickness" for "plague", a word some readers may not know.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן וְכָל־עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַלְוִיִּ֑ם כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם כֵּן־עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And did Moses and Aaron and all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel to the Levites according to all that commanded Yahweh Moses concerning the Levites; so did to them [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Moses, Aaron and the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} carried out for the Levites all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses about them; the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did exactly that with them.

L.20: And Moses and Aaron and all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did to the Levites according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses concerning the Levites; so the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did to them.

R.20: Moses, Aaron and the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses to do with the Levites. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did all of it.

decisions.choice: so they did: a closing statement of exact obedience
decisions.reason: The verse first says that Moses, Aaron and the people did everything as commanded, then says again "so the sons of Israel did to them". The repetition stresses that every part of the command was kept (compare 1:54; 9:5).

decisions.choice: did all of it
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the repeated statement but makes it short.

records.source: וַיִּֽתְחַטְּא֣וּ הַלְוִיִּ֗ם וַֽיְכַבְּסוּ֙ בִּגְדֵיהֶ֔ם וַיָּ֨נֶף אַהֲרֹ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְכַפֵּ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם אַהֲרֹ֖ן לְטַהֲרָֽם׃
records.gloss: And purified themselves from sin the Levites, and they washed their clothes, and waved Aaron them [as] a wave offering before Yahweh, and made atonement for them Aaron to cleanse them.
pieces: The Levites cleansed themselves of sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. Aaron made atonement for them so that they would be clean.

L.21: And the Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron waved them [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.

R.21: The Levites made themselves free from sin and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. He made atonement for them, so that they were clean.

decisions.choice: purified themselves from sin: removed sin and uncleanness from themselves
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for sin. In this reflexive form it means to make oneself free of sin and uncleanness, by the rites God gave (19:12-13, 20; 31:19-20). It sums up the sprinkling and shaving of verse 7.

decisions.choice: to cleanse them: the purpose of the whole rite
decisions.reason: The atonement made by the offerings of verse 12 makes the Levites clean, fit to serve at the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: presented them as a wave offering
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.source: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן בָּ֣אוּ הַלְוִיִּ֗ם לַעֲבֹ֤ד אֶת־עֲבֹֽדָתָם֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד לִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י בָנָ֑יו כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ עַל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם כֵּ֖ן עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And after so went in the Levites to serve their service in [the] tent of meeting before Aaron and before his sons; as commanded Yahweh Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.
pieces: After that the Levites went in to do their work at the tent of meeting, serving under Aaron and his sons. What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses about the Levites was done with them.

L.22: And after that the Levites went in to serve their service in the tent of meeting before Aaron and before his sons; as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.

R.22: After that the Levites began their work at the meeting tent. They worked under Aaron and his sons. Everything was done with the Levites just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses.

decisions.choice: before Aaron and before his sons: under their direction
decisions.reason: To serve "before" someone is to work in his presence and under his orders. The Levites served the priests and did not take their place (3:6-10; 18:2-3).

decisions.choice: after that the Levites went in: the command of verse 15 is fulfilled
decisions.reason: The words echo verse 15 almost exactly, showing that what was commanded there now took place.

decisions.choice: under
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "under" Aaron and his sons, the sense of the Hebrew "before" here. Literal keeps "before".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.23: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a further instruction: the ages of Levitical service
decisions.reason: This short speech (verses 24-26) adds the age at which the Levites begin and end their work.

records.heading: The ages of service for the Levites

records.source: זֹ֖את אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַלְוִיִּ֑ם מִבֶּן֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה יָבוֹא֙ לִצְבֹ֣א צָבָ֔א בַּעֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: This [is] what [is] for the Levites: from a son of five and twenty year[s] and upward he will go in to serve [the] service in [the] work of [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: "This is the rule for the Levites: from the age of twenty-five and up, each one is to come and take his place on duty in the work of the tent of meeting.

L.24: "This [is] what [applies] to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward one shall go in to perform duty in the work of the tent of meeting.

R.24: "Here is the rule for the Levites. When a Levite is twenty-five years old or older, he must come to work at the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: perform duty: serve in an organized company, as on military service
decisions.reason: The words are the verb and noun used for an army and for going out to war (1:3). Here they are used for the Levites' work at the tent, a duty done in organized groups under orders (4:3, 23, 30).

decisions.choice: from twenty-five years old: the age at which a Levite began
decisions.reason: Chapter 4 counts the Levites from thirty to fifty years old for carrying the tabernacle (4:3, 23, 30). This passage says twenty-five. The text does not explain the difference. It may be that a Levite began lighter work at twenty-five and the heavier work of carrying at thirty, or that the rule was changed later; in David's time the age was twenty (1 Chronicles 23:24, 27).

decisions.choice: he shall go in: each Levite
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, applying the rule to each Levite in turn. The Levites who served were men; the census of the Levites counted males (3:15).

decisions.choice: one shall go in
decisions.reason: Literal says "one" for the singular "he", since no person has been named; Balanced has "each one" and Readable "a Levite".

records.source: וּמִבֶּן֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה יָשׁ֖וּב מִצְּבָ֣א הָעֲבֹדָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יַעֲבֹ֖ד עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And from a son of fifty year[s] he will turn back from [the] service of the work, and not will he serve again.
pieces: But from fifty years old he is to step down from the duty of the work and serve no more.

L.25: And from fifty years old he shall withdraw from the duty of the work and shall not serve any longer.

R.25: When he is fifty years old, he must stop doing this work and not serve any longer.

decisions.choice: withdraw from the duty: retire from the regular work
decisions.reason: "Turn back from" the service means leaving it. Verse 26 shows that the older Levite still helps; what he gives up is the heavy, regular work.

decisions.choice: shall not serve any longer: no longer do the work itself
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for work or labor. Verse 26 sets it against "keeping the charge", which an older Levite may still do.

records.source: וְשֵׁרֵ֨ת אֶת־אֶחָ֜יו בְּאֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣ר מִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת וַעֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֣א יַעֲבֹ֑ד כָּ֛כָה תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לַלְוִיִּ֖ם בְּמִשְׁמְרֹתָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And he will minister with his brothers in [the] tent of meeting to keep [the] charge, but work not will he do; thus you will do to the Levites in their charges.
pieces: He may help his fellow Levites at the tent of meeting by keeping guard, but he is not to do the work. This is how you are to arrange the duties of the Levites."

L.26: And he may minister with his brothers in the tent of meeting, to keep the charge, but he shall not do work. Thus you shall do for the Levites in their duties."

R.26: He may still help the other Levites at the meeting tent by keeping watch, but he must not do the hard work. That is how you will give the Levites their jobs."

decisions.choice: keep the charge: keep watch and guard
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for the Levites' duty of guarding the tabernacle and its things so that no one unfit came near (1:53; 3:7-8, 38). It is set against "work", the labor of handling and carrying.

decisions.choice: minister with: help, attend
decisions.reason: The verb is used for serving someone of higher rank or assisting in sacred duties (3:6; 18:2). The older Levite assists the younger ones.

decisions.choice: his brothers: his fellow Levites
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means the other men of the tribe of Levi who serve with him, not only his own family.

decisions.choice: his fellow Levites / the other Levites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the "brothers" are.
